rules.statement: Persist durable, cross-session authorization records such as end-user consent in their own store keyed by their natural (tenant, client, subject) key, not as payloads in the ephemeral, consume-once grant store that logout bulk-revokes.
rules.why: The grant store holds ephemeral, single-use or expiring artifacts that end-session revokes in bulk, so consent stored there would be wiped on logout or would need special-casing and re-activation semantics.
rules.check: Look for consent or other long-lived, user-manageable authorizations written as PersistedGrant/grant-store entries, or for grant-type exclusions added to the logout revoke sweep to keep such records alive.

rules.statement: When recording a consent decision, re-resolve the pending authorization request on the server and use its client and requested scopes, never scopes or client identifiers posted by the consent form.
rules.why: Posted values can be tampered with. The server-side pending request is the authoritative source for what is being consented to.
rules.check: Look for consent POST handlers that read scopes or client id from the request body or form and pass them into the grant/persist call.

rules.statement: Resolve a pending authorization request for display (for example, a consent details endpoint) without consuming its continuation, so the request can still be resumed after the user decides.
rules.why: The details lookup must leave the parked continuation intact for the later decision and resume, the same way IdentityServer's GetAuthorizationContextAsync works.
rules.check: Look for read-only or details endpoints that call a consume/single-use retrieval on the continuation instead of a non-consuming lookup.

rules.statement: When consent is required but the authorization request has prompt=none, return the OIDC consent_required error (and audit the denial) instead of redirecting to an interactive consent surface.
rules.why: prompt=none forbids interaction, so OpenID Connect requires the consent_required error.
rules.check: Look for consent-required branches in authorize logic that redirect or challenge without first checking for prompt=none.

rules.statement: Treat existing consent as sufficient only when the recorded granted scopes cover every requested scope, and when granting, union-merge the new scopes into the existing record (an in-place upsert) instead of replacing it.
rules.why: Partial coverage must prompt the user again, and widening consent in place keeps one durable record per (tenant, client, subject).
rules.check: Look for consent checks that pass on any overlap or on record existence alone, or grant code that overwrites scopes or inserts duplicate records.

rules.statement: When an end user denies consent, answer the parked authorization request with an access_denied error at the client's redirect URI instead of just redirecting away.
rules.why: Per the amending ADR-0229, the client must be told the request was refused.
rules.check: Look for consent deny paths that redirect to a generic page or return locally without sending access_denied to the validated redirect URI.

rules.statement: When the core sends an interaction command (such as a consent challenge) that no interactive module handles, degrade to the interaction_required error instead of failing hard.
rules.why: A deployment that turns on enforcement without an interactive surface should still give the client a valid protocol response.
rules.check: Look for authorize code that throws or returns a 500 when the interaction command comes back unhandled, instead of returning interaction_required.
